rubrics.U.S. Senate / U.S. House: Job is lawmaking, oversight, budgeting and constituent service in Washington. High (75-95): prior legislative or executive office, law/judicial/prosecutorial background, deep policy or budget experience. Middle (45-70): state legislators, senior congressional or agency staff, local elected office, executive or business management. Low (10-40): no governing experience, unrelated occupation, first-time candidate with a thin record. Missing bio = null.
rubrics.Governor: Chief executive of a $120B+ state government: management of large organizations, budgets, emergency response (hurricanes), appointments, vetoes. High: prior executive office (governor, big-city mayor, agency head, Cabinet), long legislative leadership, large-organization management. Middle: legislators, lawyers, entrepreneurs with real payroll and budget experience. Low: no governing or managerial experience. Party and policy views are not scored.
rubrics.Attorney General: Chief legal officer: litigation, consumer protection, criminal appeals, opinions. High: years as a prosecutor, judge, state/federal litigator or senior government counsel plus Florida Bar standing. Middle: licensed lawyer with transferable government or legislative legal work. Low: no law license or legal practice.
rubrics.Chief Financial Officer: State CFO oversees accounting, payments, unclaimed property, insurance regulation (fraud), fire marshal. High: CPA/finance/insurance-industry leadership, public-finance or regulatory experience, running a financial institution. Middle: business owners, legislators (a committee seat doesn't add). Low: unrelated careers.
rubrics.Commissioner of Agriculture: Runs FDACS: farming policy, food safety, consumer protection, concealed-weapon licensing, state forests. High: working farmer/rancher or agribusiness operator, ag-agency or food-safety career, ag policy leadership. Middle: legislators or lawyers with consumer-protection or farm-law work. Low: no agriculture, food-safety or regulatory background.
rubrics.State Legislature (House / Senate): Job is writing law and the state budget. High (75-95): prior legislative service or chamber leadership (a committee chair doesn't add), plus law/policy/budget careers. Middle (45-70): local elected office, lawyers, policy staff, business owners and managers. Low (10-40): student/first-time with no work record, unrelated occupation. Missing info = null.
rubrics.County Commission: Land use and growth management, county budget (~$1B in Manatee), infrastructure, public safety funding. High: prior commissioner or city-manager/planner/public-administration career, plus budget and land-use experience. Middle: municipal/regional agency staff, real-estate or construction professionals with approval process knowledge, business owners. Low: unrelated occupation without public-sector exposure.
rubrics.School Board: Oversees district budget, superintendent, policy for students. High: career educator/administrator, school finance or education law, prior school board service. Middle: business managers, paid nonprofit or youth-program staff. Low: no education or governance link.
rubrics.Mosquito Control District: Independent special district: contracts and runs mosquito/vector control (adulticide, larvicide, Integrated Pest Management), budget set by tax levy, must follow state (FDACS) rules. High (80-95): pest-control/entomology/public-health/vector-control career or licensed pest-control business ownership. Middle-high (60-75): environmental/wetland/land-management professionals, public-health or biology. Middle (40-55): general public administration, small-business management. Low: unrelated. Unknown = null.
rubrics.Fire District boards: Elected commissioners oversee a fire/EMS district budget, millage, chief, stations, equipment. High: career firefighter/paramedic/fire officer or fire-service administrator, prior fire commissioner with a record. Middle: public-safety, emergency management, engineering/construction, municipal finance, business management. Low: unrelated. Unknown = null.
rubrics.CDD boards: Community Development District boards run neighborhood infrastructure (roads, ponds, amenities), assessments and a modest budget; residents sit on them. High: engineering, construction, public finance, accounting, property/facility management, prior CDD supervisor service (an HOA board doesn't count). Middle: business owners/managers, lawyers, retired executives. Low: unrelated. Most candidates have no public bio = null.
rubrics.City Council / City Commission / Mayor: City budget, zoning/land use, utilities, police/fire contracts. High: prior council or mayor service, city administration, planning, public finance, municipal law. Middle: business owners, real estate/property management, paid nonprofit management, lawyers. Low: no related work.
